summary: The mapped editorial scene succeeded: a legible hand-and-net action, fully framed dog, strong foreground fibers, and a detailed but subordinate harbor.
observations: The two hands meet at the net rather than hovering; no obvious extra fingers are visible at the inspection scale.
Warm light from the left catches the face, dog fur, rope and wet deck consistently.
The foreground net and float, seated figures, wheelhouse and harbor form four readable depth layers.
limitations: Exact lens simulation and material identity are not established by appearance alone.
Aesthetic preference is subjective; the wider scene gives less facial prominence than the source portrait.
source_comparison: The official Sunburst sailor image is a close vertical portrait with the dog behind the sailor. This adaptation deliberately widens the view and maps the action, dog and working equipment. It demonstrates greater scene breadth, not a measured improvement over an equivalent prompt.
repair_if_needed: No hard failure observed. If a face-led story were the goal, crop/framing should prioritize the portrait rather than add more background.

outcome: striking result with one layout repair recommended
observations: AFTERLIGHT, ART AFTER DARK and 19–21 OCT are all manually legible and correctly rendered.
Exactly three visitors occupy separate steps beneath a large orange disc.
Folded cobalt metal and amber glass provide a strong blue-orange material contrast.
The apex reaches the headline baseline around its center; it should have been lower for an entirely separate text zone.

source_comparison: The official Sunburst source uses a five-person streetwear photograph and a single tagline beneath the Thread wordmark. Our poster changes genre to architectural festival art and increases the exact-copy burden to three lines. It shows variety and explicit hierarchy; it is not a fair causal comparison of prompting methods.
repair_if_needed: Keep the poster, typography and colors fixed. Lower or shorten only the arch apex so the complete sculpture stays below the headline with a clear ivory-text/black gap; preserve the three visitors and exact footer.

source_comparison: The official Sunburst comparison is a warm brown bakery mark with loaf and wheat motifs on transparent pixels. This adaptation deliberately tests a simpler one-color coast/bird identity. It reduces decorative detail but is not a same-brand or same-prompt quality comparison.
repair_if_needed: Keep symbol and alpha untouched; scale only TIDELINE to about 80–85% of the symbol width and recenter. For production, rebuild the approved mark and wordmark as editable vectors and check small-size legibility.

summary: The broad historical scene follows the planned topography, five foreground figures, muddy route and distant stage. It looks plausible but remains an invented reconstruction rather than a verified historic photograph.
outcome: passes planned visible scene; historical specificity remains limited
observations: Five foreground attendees form a distinct group while the crowd descends toward the stage.
The muddy path, blankets and tents make the spatial brief readable at several depths.
The museum's cultural-landscape report confirms the bowl-shaped field and stage at the hill bottom (PDF pages 41 and 48).
limitations: No exact viewpoint, people, clothing combination, moment or stage measurements were independently matched to an archive photograph.
Distant people are too small to verify individual anatomy.
Period plausibility is not proof of complete historical accuracy.
source_comparison: The official Sunburst image emphasizes nearby faces and a stage at upper-right. Our adaptation chooses an elevated wide view, with an explicit foreground group and path leading to the distant stage. It offers spatial scale and contextual organization at the expense of close facial intimacy.
repair_if_needed: For a documentary reconstruction, choose an identified archival viewpoint and separately map the actual stage, structures and period details. Do not attempt to fix missing historical evidence by adding confident adjectives.

Panel 2 shows a white paw lifting the lid, and panel 3 shows the cat asleep on the sofa.

It successfully suppresses large dialogue but misses the final motion direction, so richer specification did not produce a fully correct story.

outcome: attractive instructional draft requiring annotation correction
observations: Cuticle, upper epidermis, palisade layer, spongy layer and lower epidermis appear in the correct top-to-bottom sequence.
The vascular bundle has larger blue xylem elements above smaller coral phloem elements.
Two green guard cells flank an opening, but the Stoma leader ends on the right guard cell rather than the opening.
The blue CO2 arrow points inward/up and the red O2 arrow outward/down; they sit outside the pore rather than clearly tracing through it.

limitations: The illustration is an enlarged schematic; no tissue scale or species-specific anatomy is established.

source_comparison: The official Sunburst source is a flat cellular-respiration overview with grouped process boxes and molecular labels. Our adaptation switches to a three-dimensional leaf cutaway grounded in OpenStax's leaf anatomy chapter. It broadens medium and subject range, but its annotation error prevents claiming a more accurate scientific result.
repair_if_needed: Move only the Stoma leader endpoint to the central pore. Remove the redundant black arrow. Route CO2 from outside through that opening into the air space and O2 in the reverse direction, keeping tissue geometry and all other labels fixed. Recheck every leader after editing.

geometry_measurement.method: Threshold the colored bar interiors inside hand-chosen plot regions; bounding boxes describe visible raster geometry, not a general chart parser.

summary: The three-chart slide renders all supplied values correctly and gives the right visual trends. Exact export dimensions and bar ratios remain slightly approximate despite explicit numeric instructions.
outcome: coherent data graphic; fails strict pixel and ratio precision
observations: All trip counts, on-time percentages, category percentages and the fictional-data footer are manually legible and correct.
Trips bar heights measured 190, 283 and 380 pixels, close to but not exactly 1:1.5:2.
March mix lengths measured 318, 193 and 130 pixels, close to but not exactly 5:3:2.

limitations: The strict failures are small geometric/export deviations, not wrong printed data or reversed trends.
Color-threshold measurements are scoped to this image and count bar interiors; antialiasing can move a boundary by a pixel.
Generated charts remain raster pictures, not editable data-bound charts.
No general statement about mathematical accuracy follows from one sample.
source_comparison: The official Sunburst market slide has concentric market-size circles and one bar chart, using fictional inputs. Our adaptation gives three explicit chart specifications and complete synthetic data. It better exposes whether pixels follow the numbers: labels succeed while geometric ratios remain approximate. This is a diagnostic comparison, not evidence of model or prompt superiority.
repair_if_needed: For a concept slide, these small deviations may be acceptable if declared. For exact chart publication, render the fixed dataset with a plotting or slide tool and preserve the approved visual styling; set exact 16:9 dimensions with an output setting or deterministic canvas. Do not spend repeated image generations chasing single-pixel chart ratios.
